data.name: Abram
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Abram means 'exalted father'. In the Old Testament, Abram is the name given to Abraham before God changed it to 'father of many'.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the spiritual journey of transformation and fatherhood.

biblical_reference.note: The patriarch Abraham, considered the founder of the Jewish people, is the protagonist of the Book of Genesis in the Hebrew Bible and the Old Testament of the Christian Bible.

saint_reference.note: Abram is not a recognized saint in any major denomination.

data.cultural_impact: The name Abram has had significant cultural impact in history, particularly in the Middle East and among the Jewish and Christian communities. Abraham is considered a patriarch and a founding figure in both Judaism and Christianity, and is mentioned frequently in the Bible. His name is celebrated in various holy texts and religious traditions, and has survived thousands of years and spread around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: Abram, or Abraham as he is more commonly known, is often referred to as the father of faith. The story of Abraham's obedience and trust in God has been an inspiring example to millions of believers throughout history. He left his home and family to follow God's call, demonstrating faith and trust in the divine plan. His willingness to sacrifice his only son, Isaac, when God requested it, is a testament to his devotion and dedication to God. The name Abram serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in God, and the spiritual journey that comes with it.
